mentions.market_hint: Marco Rubio wins 2028 US presidential election
mentions.cleaned_quote: Kalshi has Marco Rubio number one at 21 percent, Gavin Newsom 18, JD Vance 18. Tim Miller said he'd fade Rubio hard. I agree Rubio probably won't be president in 2028 — I took the no on him in yesterday's draft intentionally. But fading it hard isn't wise: your upside is only 21 percent over three years, about 7 percent APY. Think APY every time.

mentions.market_hint: Donald Trump Jr. wins 2028 GOP presidential nomination (long-shot value)
mentions.cleaned_quote: The only way to get a really good investment in the 2028 market is on real long shots — like a Donald Trump Jr., who I mentioned yesterday. A guy who might pop up if he announces or starts whispering about announcing. There could be some money there potentially.

mentions.market_hint: Average US gas price exceeds $5/$6/$7 (oil/gas hedge strategy)
mentions.cleaned_quote: My gas-price hedge: take yes on a market for gas going over $5, $6, or $7. If gas stays low you win at the pump; if it spikes the market pays you and offsets the higher cost. Since I first talked about it, many of you piled in and the futures contracts have run up, making it harder to offset right now. You can also do it with a fund like DBO that tracks oil.

Will Jesus come back by 2030? People put no because if he comes back they'll be happy — good hedging-your-life situation. But you only get 10 percent, spread over five years. That's not that great. You have to think about the timeframe, not just the amount.

mentions.market_hint: LA mayoral race — Spencer Pratt vs leading candidate after debate
mentions.cleaned_quote: In the LA mayoral race, the leading candidate did poorly in the debate. Before any poll or punditry, prediction markets quantified what we saw — Spencer Pratt did well and she sank like 40 points. That's worse than Joe Biden's 15-point drop after his 2024 debate. Part of the job of these markets is to bring information to you faster.
